questions.prompt: A VM is in West Europe. You move it to a resource group whose metadata location is North Europe using the standard ARM move operation. Where does the VM run afterward?

options.explanation: Changing resource-group membership does not change the VM region.
Resource-group metadata location does not control member resource locations.
An ARM scope move does not configure replication.

options.text: A region chosen from the destination group name
options.explanation: Names do not select the physical region of an existing VM.

questions.prompt: You plan an ARM cross-subscription VM move. Which TWO requirements should you validate?

options.text: Both subscriptions belong to the same Entra tenant.
options.explanation: Direct ARM moves do not cross tenant boundaries.

options.text: The virtual network and required dependent resources are included as required.
options.explanation: Cross-subscription VM moves have dependency requirements.

options.text: Only the VM resource is needed regardless of its dependencies.
options.explanation: Networking and other resource dependencies can block validation.

options.text: The move automatically changes the VM to the destination group region.
options.explanation: Scope moves preserve the VM region.

questions.prompt: After a successful VM move to another resource group, an automation script using the old resource ID fails. What should be checked first?

options.text: Update the script to use the VM resource ID at its new scope.
options.explanation: The resource-group segment of the ID changes during the move.

options.text: Assume the VM has retained the old ID permanently.
options.explanation: A resource ID includes its resource group.

options.text: Change only the guest hostname to match the old resource group.
options.explanation: Guest hostname does not repair an ARM resource ID reference.

options.text: Reinstall the VM agent to recreate the old resource ID.
options.explanation: The agent does not determine the VM ARM scope.
